_comment: Weather and the dark, per biome (WRSurvival; cooks/build-survival.md, survival-crafting 2.4, world-map 2.6). Each biome rolls every rollMinutes: one weather at a time, by chance (dayOnly / nightOnly respected), announced warnSeconds ahead (the toast, the fog closing in from the horizon, the bed rising), ramping in over rampSeconds and out over fadeSeconds. effects reach a player only outdoors (a roof within counters.roofWithin cm, a cave) and not countered (resist = infused armour frost / lava, armor ids, pathNodes path.node, items carried). No temperature meter: every effect is a gear check or a change in what you can see (DD Ruled out). look: fx / baseFx thicken the falling weather at the camera, fogDensity and fogColor (sRGB) the haze, skyDim the sun, glyph the HUD's Data/UI/Glyphs icon. darkNights: unlit at night outside a light; underground: unlit anywhere outside a light; corruption.path: the path that gains instead of suffering. Only volcanic and tundra exist on the island today; the other rows switch on when their land does.

kinds.name: Ashfall
kinds.does: Ash chokes the air: about 60 m to see, thirst x1.25 in the open, outdoor crops stop growing. A roof, or Forgeplate, keeps it off.

kinds.name: Overcast
kinds.does: Grey skies: dimmer light.

kinds.name: Rain
kinds.does: Rain: torches burn faster; a roof keeps it off.

kinds.name: Eruption
kinds.does: The volcano is erupting: ash to 80 m, lava bombs fall round anyone outdoors near the crater (the boom, then a glow where it lands). Get under a roof or away from the crater.

kinds.name: Blizzard
kinds.does: Whiteout: about 40 m to see, deep snow slows your run, stamina returns slower in the open, Gloomhowls hunt from further. A roof or frost gear holds it off.

kinds.name: Snowfall
kinds.does: Heavy snow: about 200 m to see.

kinds.name: Freezing fog
kinds.does: Freezing fog: you can see about 70 m; creatures notice you later.

kinds.name: Overcast
kinds.does: Grey skies: dimmer light.

kinds.name: Whiteout
kinds.coming: A white wall is rolling off the glacier
kinds.does: Whiteout: 25 m to see, gusts off the glacier, deep drifts slow you; Gloomhowls hunt by day. Shrine fires and camp lamps still show.

kinds.name: Thunderstorm
kinds.does: Lightning seeks the highest body above 600 m: a glow under your feet, then the bolt a second later; gusts shove you on the heights. Get low, get under rock, or carry a grounding charm.

kinds.name: Overcast
kinds.does: Grey skies: dimmer light.

kinds.name: Rain
kinds.does: Rain: torches burn faster; a roof keeps it off.

kinds.name: Fog
kinds.does: Fog: you can see about 70 m; creatures notice you later.

kinds.name: Heat wave
kinds.coming: The air is starting to shimmer over the sand
kinds.does: Heat wave: thirst x2 in direct sun (any roof, overhang, palm or a big rock's shadow is shade); mirage water shimmers on the Pan. Dunewrap (2 pieces) or a sand veil keep it off; carry water. Sun walkers fill Radiance x1.2.
kinds._why: cooks/biome-desert.md 2.9: world-map's 30 weight and x2 win over survival-crafting's 35 / x1.5 (logged to LATER-COOKS by the design cook).

kinds.name: Sandstorm
kinds.coming: A brown wall is rising over the Spine
kinds.does: Sandstorm: the belt's storm over the whole desert: you see 25 m, run x0.7, Radiance doesn't fill, and the compass ribbon hides (a Sunwatch lens or a tame Scarab digger shows the way). A sand veil or Dunewrap (4) halve the slow and let you see 60 m. After it, sunstone grows half again, and the sand has shifted off old doors.
kinds._why: cooks/biome-desert.md 2.8-2.9: the haboob rolls west off the Spine; WRDesertHazards gives it the belt's rules over the whole desert, WRDesertWorld its plenty (+50% sunstone) and the Lee Door.

kinds.name: Overcast
kinds.coming: High dust cloud is coming over
kinds.does: High dusty cloud: dimmer light; Radiance fills slower (x0.6).

kinds.name: Rain
kinds._why: cooks/biome-forest.md 2.9 (the signature): every outdoor plot irrigated and crops +25% (WRForestHazards::CropScale), Truffler finds x2, torches and burns last half as long, under the F4/F5 canopy the rain comes as heavy drips 20 s late, the Alder spates (WRForestHazards), Mossmauls and Rootcoils hunt by day.
kinds.does: Rain: outdoor crops are watered and grow faster; torches and thornbrake burns last half as long; the Alder will run high and brown (its fords push you downstream). A roof keeps it off.

kinds.name: Morning mist
kinds._why: cooks/biome-forest.md 2.9: only 05:00-10:00; sight 70 m on the floor (the canopy stands above it); Thornlynx drop from 1.5x range; resin +50% (the plenty after rain: WRForestHazards::GatherScale).
kinds.coming: Mist is gathering on the forest floor
kinds.does: Morning mist: about 70 m to see under the trees; Thornlynx drop on you from further off; weeping resin runs thick (+50%).

kinds.name: Overcast
kinds._why: cooks/biome-forest.md 2.9: flat light; the Elder Canopy goes from dusk to near-dark and the foxfire shows by day. Clear (the other 35%) is no weather: light shafts and finch flocks.
kinds.does: Grey skies: the deep wood goes nearly dark, and the foxfire shows by day.

biomes.name: Sky islands
biomes._why: cooks/biome-sky.md 2.6: Clear 45 (no weather), Overcast 10, Rain 10, Cloud fog 15, Gale 20.

kinds.name: Gale front
kinds.coming: The wind is rising: torn cloud racing in from the east
kinds.does: Gusts everywhere above 300 m every 4 to 8 s (the whistle 1.5 s before; the grass and cloth snap). Brace (crouch or guard) for half the shove; anchor boots or Skysilk 4 hold you. Torches blow out; gliders drift hard downwind; Skyrays breach at dusk.
kinds._why: cooks/biome-sky.md 2.6: Gale 20. The gusts are WRSkyAir's (hazards.sky.gale: cells above 300 m, 4-8 s, 1,200 cm/s for 0.8 s, 1.5 s tell), not the generic weather gust.

kinds.name: Cloud fog
kinds.does: The islands under 800 m sit inside cloud: about 40 m to see. Hushwings hunt by day in it; Mistlarks call to find each other (follow them to the updrafts).

kinds.name: Rain
kinds.does: Rain from above: waterfalls run double, gossamer hangs heavy (drifts give twice the Skysilk); torches burn faster; a roof keeps it off.

kinds.name: Overcast
kinds.does: Flat white light; the cloud sea rises 100 m and the Skyrays drift lower, into the Cloud Gardens.

kinds.name: Overcast
kinds.does: Grey skies: dimmer light.

kinds.name: Rain
kinds.does: Rain: drips sing in the upper geode halls (the crystals glow brighter, the bats hear less); resonant crystal yields more after.

kinds.name: Fog
kinds.does: Sea fog over the plateau: the chime arches ring in the damp. Underground it changes nothing.

kinds.name: Overcast
kinds.does: Grey skies: flat light; the falls' red reads strongest.

kinds.name: Rain
kinds.does: Rain: bleedwater pools spread a little wider, plank creaks carry further, crops count as watered; torches burn faster.

kinds.name: Fog
kinds.does: Thick fog: about 30 m to see; Murkjaws and Bogstalkers strike from twice as far. Light still carries: a lantern or a Lanterntoad shows the way.

kinds.name: Miasma
kinds.coming: A red haze is rising off the pools
kinds.does: An oxblood fog: about 40 m to see. Murkjaws hunt the water by the boardwalks, Hexcrow curse cries carry half as far again, and corpse candles burn by day.

biomes.name: Ocean and reefs

kinds.name: Squall
kinds.coming: A squall is building over the reef
kinds.does: Squall: driving rain and a gale, swells two and three metres high. Swimming on the surface costs half again the stamina; the man o' war fleets blow inshore and strand on the strand; Reefjaws come in twice as thick at sea. Lightning flashes, but it never strikes the land. After it, the wreck tide.
kinds._why: cooks/biome-ocean.md 2.9: world-map's weights stand (Squall 15); no strikes on land or within 600 m of shore. The open-sea mast strike waits for boats (LATER-COOKS).

kinds.name: Sea fog
kinds.does: Sea fog: you can see 60 to 80 m and under the water half as far. Most things notice you later, but the Gullraiders hunt in it. A lit Beacon Stack cuts through it.

kinds.name: Rain
kinds.coming: Rain coming in off the sea
kinds.does: Rain: the sea's surface pocks (wakes and fins are harder to see), fish bite sooner, torches burn faster; a roof keeps it off.

kinds.name: Overcast
kinds.does: Overcast: grey light; under the water you see a fifth less far, and the Pound's sun mirrors throw half a beam.

biomes._why: cooks/biome-ocean.md 2.9: Clear 40 (what's left), Overcast 15, Rain 15, Sea fog 15, Squall 15.

kinds.name: Corpse fog
kinds.coming: A pale fog is rising off the graves
kinds.does: Every light reaches only seven tenths as far. Bigger lights, or Gravecloth.

kinds.name: Ground mist
kinds.coming: Mist is gathering in the hollows
kinds.does: Knee-deep mist over the graves: about 80 m to see, and creatures notice you later. Buried hounds' mounds hide in it.

kinds.name: Overcast
kinds.does: Grey skies: dimmer light.

kinds.name: Drizzle
kinds.coming: A cold drizzle is coming in
kinds.does: Drizzle: torches burn faster, crops count as watered, and the lime pits boil (twice the burn).

biomes.name: Fungal caverns
biomes._why: cooks/biome-fungal.md 2.9 (world-map KEPT weights): Clear 30 (no weather), Overcast 20, Rain 20, Spore drift 30, on the surface only (the caverns are under rock: sheltered). The Spore bloom is the caverns' own 20-minute clock (WRFungalHazards, tuning hazards.fungal.bloom), not a weather.

kinds.name: Overcast
kinds.does: Grey skies over the cape: the Breath over the Great Doline reads strongest against them.

kinds.name: Rain
kinds.does: Rain pours into the dolines as waterfalls. It knocks spores down: no spore clouds form in the open while it falls.

kinds.name: Spore drift
kinds.does: Every doline breathes out spores: thin clouds drift 200 m downwind of each (you see 20 m inside). A filter mask, a spore wad or Sporeweave keeps them out.

kinds.name: Grey wind
kinds.does: Corruption builds twice as fast in the open. Stay by a brazier or under a roof; Gravecloth or Hollowplate holds it off.

kinds.name: Overcast
kinds.does: Grey skies: dimmer light.

kinds.name: Dead calm
kinds.does: No wind, no sound: your own steps carry, and the blind hunters hear you from further. Walk softly; crouch past them.
